name: devices-random-xorshift
title: tests(devices): pin Random read xorshift64 sequence and state advancement
body:
### What
Pins `DeviceRegistry::read` Random xorshift64 sequence: first four bytes match the reference algorithm from default seed, and successive reads advance state.

### Why it matters
The PRNG drives /dev/random output; replacing XOR with OR or flipping shift direction produces a degenerate or predictable stream. Existing tests verify read succeeds but never pin output values.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `^= ... << 13` -> `\|= ... << 13` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `<< 13` -> `>> 13` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-devices --lib random_read_pins`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

name: vfs-copy-overlay-size-boundary
title: tests(vfs): pin copy_to_overlay exact FILE_SIZE acceptance
body:
### What
Pins `copy_to_overlay` size gate: exact FILE_SIZE fit copies successfully, and smaller base files also copy without rejection.

### Why it matters
Relaxing `>` to `>=` rejects valid exact-fit images; relaxing to `==` admits only exact sizes and rejects all smaller files. Existing tests never exercise the overlay copy size boundary.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `size > FILE_SIZE` -> `size >= FILE_SIZE` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `size > FILE_SIZE` -> `size == FILE_SIZE` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-vfs --lib copy_to_overlay_accepts`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.
spec_ref: overlay copy-on-write size invariant (VFS internal contract)

name: fs-policy-identity-token-fnv1a
title: tests(fs-policy): pin identity_token to exact FNV-1a reference hashes
body:
### What
Pins `identity_token` to exact FNV-1a reference hashes for empty, rocky, and peer inputs.

### Why it matters
Instance identity tokens gate capability separation; changing the XOR accumulation to AND/OR produces different hashes that still pass stability/separation checks but break cross-component identity agreement. Existing tests verify properties, not exact values.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `^=` -> `&=` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `^=` -> `|=` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-fs-policy --lib identity_token_matches_fnv1a`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.
